title: Job
description: The durable unit of work that carries a FULLY RESOLVED semantic operation from the control plane toward the Blender Worker. project_id is mandatory: a worker must never modify another project's Blender file (see .kiro/steering/security.md), so a job is not representable without it. job_type is the discriminator: each type binds to exactly one payload schema via the conditionals below, which keeps Job typed rather than an untyped dictionary. Two identities are distinguished: job_id is the stable identity of THIS job record (and the execution identity a worker deduplicates deliveries on), while idempotency_key is the MUTATION identity derived from the originating request. By the time a Job exists, units and directions are already resolved into canonical meters and explicit coordinates.

job_id.description: Stable identifier for this job attempt.

payload.description: Operation-specific data. Constrained by job_type in the conditionals below.

status.description: Lifecycle state. queued -> claimed -> running -> succeeded | failed.

idempotency_key.description: Deterministic MUTATION IDENTITY, derived from (project_id, origin.request_id, origin.operation_index) — never from the payload contents. Two intentional submissions of the same instruction differ here and both execute; a retry of one submission matches an existing job and executes once. Uniqueness is scoped per project.

content_fingerprint.description: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. A canonical hash of (job_type, payload), useful for spotting repeated or accidental duplicate operations in logs and tests. It is deliberately NOT the mutation identity: identical content from two distinct requests is legitimate and must execute twice.

result.description: Operation result, present only on success. Unconstrained at the contract level.

allOf.description: job_type discriminates the payload. Adding an operation means adding a payload schema and one conditional here.
inspect_scene is a READ job: its payload is empty and closed, because the project is already trusted job identity and there is nothing else to select.
A failed job MUST carry a structured error; any other state MUST NOT.
A claimed or running job MUST carry worker ownership metadata.
A queued job MUST NOT be owned by a worker yet.
Only a succeeded job may carry a result.
